correctness.rationale: The primary article's Proposition 4 gives the frozen normalization: the hazard is x^(alpha−1) R_0(x)/m_alpha(x), and the common density/survival normalizer cancels. The exact model formulas use the frozen scales. For the two baselines, put nu=−1 (half-normal) or nu=1 (Maxwell). Their survival is asymptotic to a positive constant times x^nu exp(−x²/(2 beta²)); comparison with each exact density gives baseline hazard h_0(x)~x/beta² without differentiating a big-O error. Both q=beta² x^(alpha−2) R_0(x) and m_alpha tend to zero, m_alpha' is everywhere negative, and q'/m_alpha'=beta² h_0(x)/x−beta²(alpha−2)/x²→1. Hence q/m_alpha→1 and the transformed hazard tends to infinity on the right with the stated equivalent. Tonelli applied to X_0^alpha=∫_0^{X_0} alpha t^(alpha−1) dt gives the finite strictly positive m_alpha(0); lower-endpoint continuity gives the second equivalent. Right divergence excludes even nonincreasing behavior. For 0<alpha<1 both ends diverge, so minimizing on a compact subinterval cut off above a fixed interior value gives an interior global minimum. The hazard is nonconstant real analytic on (0,infinity), so such a minimum is also an actual local turn. The independent tail-moment calculation at alpha=0.1, beta=1 finds local minima near 0.7925118344 and 0.6556500382 and reproduces the hazard values at those points and at 0.1 and 10.
residual_risks: The numeric stationary-point checks do not certify uniqueness, the numerical location of the global minimum, or a full monotonicity classification. None is required by the analytic assertions.

evidence: Resultary 9f38807432e0 excludes global decrease for a right-truncated exponentiated Ailamujia law through h(x)~1/(1−x) at a finite boundary. The IHSB article itself lists decreasing hazards for the two Gaussian-tail models.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The right-truncation mechanism comes from an interval of integration shrinking to zero at a hard endpoint, not from a Gaussian decay rate at infinity. That finding is neither equivalent to the IHSB asymptotic nor a general theorem covering it. The primary article's formula is identical but its qualitative conclusion is different.

value.rationale: This answers a concrete error in how two published lifetime models can be used: neither can represent globally decreasing failure rates. One analytic tail mechanism settles all shape and scale parameters and explains why a descending segment on a finite window cannot establish global decrease. For shapes below one it additionally proves the existence of a turn without relying on optimization of a plotted curve.
residual_risks: This does not classify critical points or prove global increase for any remaining parameter range.
